source: sam3d game values; levels are estimates (docs/fx/README.md section 4.2), each named below
notes: How the weapons and the aircraft sound (USimFxAudioSubsystem, unreal/SAM3D/Source/SAM3D/Private/SimFxAudio.cpp). Every sample is an asset /Game/SAM3D/FX/Sounds/<sample>.<sample>, made by tools/ue_make_fx_assets.py from art/fx/sounds/<sample>.wav (tools/fx_sounds.py, its SOUNDS). A level is the sound pressure level 1 m from the source (dB re 20 uPa) before spreading, the air's absorption and the ground; an explosion's comes from simcore's fx::PeakSplDb by its charge instead. The game hears each source where it was when the sound now arriving left it (simcore/fx/acoustics.hpp) and plays the loudest through a loudness window.

mix.source: sam3d game value: the loudness window as in Frostbite's HDR audio; peak_to_level_db sets a blast's peak level against an engine's running level (an estimate)

propagation.source: sam3d game value: the near and far samples crossfade between near_m and far_m (as Arma 3's distance sets); a voice is placed voice_distance_m along the line to where the sound left (the engine only pans it)

enclosure.source: estimate (sam3d): the Osa's closed cabin muffles what is outside to a dull thud; what stands beside the vehicle comes through the hull less muffled

turbojet_fighter.source: estimate: an F-35 at 305 m at military power 115 dB is about 165 dB at 1 m aft, an F-16 about 160 dB (FX research C6); a turbojet taken 2 dB louder, its whine 16 dB under the roar (sam3d game value). Far off (propagation near_m to far_m) the recorded military jet (NPS) takes over the synthesised roar at the roar's 162 dB plus its match (recordings), so the crossfade holds the loudness

turbofan_fighter.source: estimate: an F-16-class fighter about 160 dB at 1 m aft (FX research C6); the fan's whine louder than a turbojet's (sam3d game value). Far off the recorded military jet (NPS) at the roar's 160 dB plus its match (recordings)

heavy_jet.source: estimate (sam3d): four large engines, a slower and lower roar than a fighter's at about its level (158 dB): the recorded 747SP (NASA SOFIA) at 158 dB plus its match (recordings); the synthesised fan whine near only (the recording has its own)

turboprop.source: estimate (sam3d): the propellers' blade-pass drone (148 dB) and the turbines' whine; the drone is the recorded An-24 (its AI-24s are the An-26's family) at 148 dB plus its match (recordings)

helicopter.source: estimate (sam3d): the main rotor's slap (146 dB) and the turboshafts' whine. The slap is the recorded Chinook played 1.4 times faster (its 10.4 blade slaps a second to 14.6: an AH-1's are 10.8, a Mi-8's 16, a Mi-24's 20), far off the recorded helicopter over a lake; each at 146 dB plus its match (recordings)

piston.source: estimate (sam3d): one radial engine and its propeller (An-2, a light trainer)

cruise_turbojet.source: estimate (sam3d): a small turbojet or turbofan (a drone, a Tomahawk's F107) far quieter than a fighter's and higher

rocket_small.source: estimate: a 20 kN motor with a 2200 m/s exhaust, Lp about 159 dB at 1 m by Eldred's rule (FX research C6); the sustainer's lower thrust 6 dB down (sam3d game value). Far off the recorded Atlas V heard from afar (NASA) played 1.8 times faster (a small motor's roar peaks higher), at 159 dB plus its match (recordings)

rocket_large.source: estimate (sam3d): a large liquid or solid motor (the Kh-22's) by Eldred's rule scaled up from the 20 kN case (168 dB). The recorded SLS test fire (NASA) near and the Shuttle's launch heard from afar (NASA) far, played a little faster (smaller motors than those), each at 168 dB plus its match (recordings)

fire.source: estimate (sam3d): a burning wreck's roar and crackle

models.source: sam3d game value: each basic model's engines (data/scenery/basic_models.json): MiG-21/23/25/27, Su-17/22/24/25 and F-4 turbojets; F-15, F-16, F-111, Tornado and A-10 turbofans; the Kh-22 a liquid rocket

archetypes.source: sam3d game value: a model with no entry of its own sounds as its archetype; a jet longer than heavy_jet_length_m as a heavy jet

missiles.source: sam3d game value: a missile whose munition has no motor data burns this long; a site's missile (no entity) longer than large_from_length_m (the S-75's, the S-200's) sounds as a large rocket; one with no flight time given flies at flyer_mps to its aim

events.source: estimate (sam3d): launch levels by Eldred's rule as the motors (FX research C6) with the igniter's crack; a GP bomb's fill about 42 % of its mass (Mk 82: 89 kg of 227 kg, FX research C6); an aircraft's fuel fireball (the picture's, LOOK 6) a combustion roar, not a jet's: 150 dB at 1 m, under a fighter's roar and far under the blast before it; the rest game values. A flare's pop (S_FX_Flare_Pop, tools/fx_sounds.py) and an air-to-air missile off its rail (the launch sample pitched up, a smaller motor than a SAM's) are game values by ear (roadmap B13), a salvo heard as at most flare_pops_max pops. The rockets' and bombs' ripples (their intervals and how many) and the guns' bursts are the picture's, data/fx/effects.json's bombs and guns; a flak shell's charge and a gun's rate and muzzle speed the munition's (data/scenery/munitions.json), flak_default_kg when it has none

blast_source: sam3d game value: the charge classes of tools/fx_sounds.py's explosions; within a class a bigger charge plays lower, (ref_kg / charge)^blast_pitch_exponent. Far off (the far half of the crossfade) a blast of 3 kg or more rolls on under the recorded NPS thunder's roll (tail, from tail_delay_s, tail_db under the blast): set so that 1-3 s in the roll sits 6-10 dB under the synthesised far blast and carries on after it has died (its RMS in 1 s windows against S_FX_Explosion_*_Far's, measured with tools/fx_sounds.py's read_wav)

recordings.source: art/fx/recorded/PROVENANCE.md 2 (NASA, NPS: public domain; Wikimedia Commons: public domain or CC0), made into the bank by tools/fx_sounds.py. recorded_at_m: how far off each was made, an estimate (sam3d) from the source's description and its spectrum (what the air had already taken off it): the game dulls it only by the rest of the way (NASA's press sites are 5-6 km from the pads; the NPS jet 'far off' has nothing left above 1 kHz; the SLS test, SOFIA, the An-24 and the Chinook keep their highs, so were near). match_db: the recording's level against the synthesised sound it stands for, both heard as the game plays them at at_m (pitch, the air's low-pass there less the recording's own distance), so the recording's layer is stands_for_level_db_1m + match_db and the crossfade holds the sourced level; tools/fx_sounds.py --check recomputes each and fails past 1 dB

guns.source: estimate (sam3d): no muzzle-blast data for 23 mm or larger was found (FX research C6); rates from the guns' cyclic rates (FX research G: 23 mm 850-1000 rounds a minute a barrel, S-60 70 practical, M61 6000, GAU-8 3900); muzzle speeds FX research G. A munition's own rate and muzzle speed (data/scenery/munitions.json) win where it has them; a pass fires in the picture's bursts (effects.json guns: SimFxLogic::GunBursts on the event's seq); the fighters' guns in the air battle (roadmap B13: m61a1 to mg127, air_combat.json's ids) by their cyclic rates (M61 6000, GSh-23L 3400, GSh-6-23 9000, GSh-30-2 3000, ADEN 1300, BK 27 1700, NR-30 900, 12.7 mm 1200 rounds a minute, operator-country reference pages; levels by ear) for the burst's seconds; an aircraft's gun for as long as the picture's gun run (its rounds at the rate, 0.5-4 s)

booms.source: sam3d game value: Carlson's shape factor 0.1 for a fighter at cruise weight (simcore/fx/acoustics.hpp, NASA TP-1122 as there); a fighter's or a missile's boom short, a big aircraft's long
